chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The Tashahhud in the voluntary prayer is part of the Tashahhud of the obligatory prayer."

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدُ: Tashahhud: The sitting position in prayer where the testimony of faith is recited.
key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: Nafl: Voluntary or supererogatory prayers performed in addition to the obligatory ones.
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: Fard: Obligatory prayers required of every Muslim.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the Tashahhud in voluntary prayers compared to obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Tashahhud in voluntary prayers is a subset of the obligatory one, reflecting the Shia scholarly consensus that while the full formal testimony (including specific salutations upon the Prophet and Imams) is required in Fard, the core declaration of faith in Nafl suffices. This ruling underscores the principle of simplicity in voluntary acts of worship while maintaining continuity with the structure of the primary prayer.
